text: {"distance_m": 1.2, "reasoning_short": "At 5% contrast the spot must subtend about 3 arcmin to be seen. 1 mm ÷ 3 arcmin (8.7×10⁻⁴ rad) ≈ 1.15 m, so roughly 1.2 m. This is a rough estimate: a black spot (100% contrast) is detectable at about 0.5–1 arcmin. For small spots, detection depends on contrast × area (Ricco's law), so threshold diameter scales as 1/√contrast, about 4.5× larger at 5%."}
